html: The school Plato founded around 387 BCE in a grove just outside Athens, named after the hero Academus. Aristotle studied there for twenty years. The school ended when the Roman general Sulla sacked Athens in 86 BCE. Philosophers who taught Plato's ideas in Athens later carried on its name until the emperor Justinian closed the pagan schools in 529 CE.
